claims.text: Conventional metallic components such as steel rollers and guide plates undergo rapid corrosion during prolonged contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
A dense Al2O3 coating can be deposited on equipment components by thermal spraying or physical vapor deposition.
The deposited Al2O3 coating will form a continuous barrier at the interface with molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 barrier will be non-wettable by molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 barrier will prevent direct chemical reaction between the metallic substrate and molten aluminum.
The Al2O3 barrier will restrict diffusion between the metallic substrate and molten aluminum.
Alumina is chemically inert and resistant to attack by molten aluminum at hot-dip processing temperatures.
Reduced wetting and chemical attack will limit corrosion and degradation of the underlying metallic substrate.
Al2O3-coated components will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Al2O3-coated components will have a longer service life than uncoated components under identical process conditions.
Coating effectiveness depends on coating uniformity, adhesion quality, and resistance to thermal cycling.
Severe thermal stresses or coating defects may limit the protection afforded by the Al2O3 coating.
Repeated thermal cycling and mechanical stress may compromise the long-term adhesion and integrity of the Al2O3 coating.
